newsitem.title: USA: Rawlings says low baseball sales hurt Q1 revenues.
newsitem.headline: Rawlings says low baseball sales hurt Q1 revenues.

text.p: Rawlings Sporting Goods Inc said Tuesday a slump in the sales of baseball-related products and basketballs helped cause a loss of $0.01 per share in the first quarter of fiscal 1997.
Rawlings reported net income of $0.12 in the first quarter of fiscal 1996.

The copmany said the decrease in revenues from baseballs is primarily tied to the significant contribution of Cal Ripken commemorative baseballs in the year-ago period. Rawlings added its customers also continued a trend toward later shipments for baseball gloves and a major warehouse club also decided to exit the baseball category.
Rawlings officials said the company is well positioned to take advantage of a strong selling season this spring.
The company makes sporting goods equipment.
Its shares were down 2/16 Tuesday afternoon at 10-15/16.
